title: Maintenance input record layout
rule: Each INPFILE record is 53 bytes: column 1 is the action code, columns 2-3 the two-character transaction type code and columns 4-53 the 50-character description. Short records are padded with spaces.
fields: INPUT-REC-TYPE, INPUT-REC-NUMBER, INPUT-REC-DESC (WS-INPUT-REC, COBTUPDT working storage)

test.then: INPUT-REC-TYPE = `A`, INPUT-REC-NUMBER = `04`, INPUT-REC-DESC = `Authorization` followed by 37 spaces

title: Open-file status message
rule: On start the program opens INPFILE and displays `OPEN FILE OK` when the file status is `00`, otherwise `OPEN FILE NOT OK`.

test.given: an existing INPFILE (even an empty one)
test.then: the second SYSOUT line is `OPEN FILE OK`

title: Open failure does not stop the program
rule: If the open fails the program still falls through into the read loop; there is no stop, return code or abend on `OPEN FILE NOT OK`. With no end-of-file condition ever raised the loop would keep reporting invalid records (see Findings F2; derived from the source, not executed).

test.given: INPFILE cannot be opened (file status not `00`)
test.then: `OPEN FILE NOT OK` is displayed and control continues into 1001-READ-NEXT-RECORDS anyway

title: Read loop and record echo
rule: Records are read sequentially until end of file. Every record read (not the end-of-file read) is echoed as `PROCESSING   ` (three spaces) followed by the full 53-byte record, before it is acted on.

test.then: SYSOUT shows `PROCESSING   U02Payment - bank transfer` padded with trailing spaces to 53 record bytes, then `UPDATING RECORD`

title: Empty input file
rule: An empty INPFILE is not an error: after `OPEN FILE OK` nothing else is displayed by COBTUPDT, no SQL is issued and the step ends with return code 0.

test.then: SYSOUT from COBTUPDT is only `OPEN FILE OK`; table rows are unchanged by COBTUPDT; RC 0

title: Action A inserts a new transaction type
rule: Action code `A` displays `ADDING RECORD` and inserts a row into CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE with TR_TYPE = columns 2-3 and TR_DESCRIPTION = columns 4-53.
fields: INPUT-REC-TYPE, INPUT-REC-NUMBER, INPUT-REC-DESC (WS-INPUT-REC, COBTUPDT working storage)

test.then: `ADDING RECORD` is displayed and a row 05 / `Refund` (space-padded to 50) exists

title: Insert success message
rule: When the INSERT returns SQLCODE 0 the program displays `RECORD INSERTED SUCCESSFULLY`.

test.then: SYSOUT shows `ADDING RECORD` then `RECORD INSERTED SUCCESSFULLY`; RC stays 0

title: Description stored space-padded to 50 characters
rule: INSERT and UPDATE bind the fixed PIC X(50) field INPUT-REC-DESC, not the DCLGEN VARCHAR structure, so TR_DESCRIPTION is stored with trailing spaces to its full 50 characters. Rows written by other means (seed data, dynamic SQL) are not padded.

test.then: TR_DESCRIPTION = `Fee` + 47 spaces (50 characters), whereas a seed row such as `Purchase` has no padding

title: Action U updates a description by key
rule: Action code `U` displays `UPDATING RECORD` and sets TR_DESCRIPTION to columns 4-53 for the row whose TR_TYPE equals columns 2-3.
fields: INPUT-REC-TYPE, INPUT-REC-NUMBER, INPUT-REC-DESC (WS-INPUT-REC, COBTUPDT working storage)

test.then: row 02 has TR_DESCRIPTION `Payment - bank transfer` padded to 50

title: Update success message
rule: When the UPDATE returns SQLCODE 0 the program displays `RECORD UPDATED SUCCESSFULLY`.

test.then: SYSOUT shows `UPDATING RECORD` then `RECORD UPDATED SUCCESSFULLY`

title: Update of a missing key
rule: The source treats UPDATE SQLCODE +100 (no row) as an error: it displays `No records found.` and sets return code 4. Off-host, Open COBOL ESQL is expected to report SQLCODE 0 for a zero-row UPDATE as it does for DELETE (BR-TT-014), which would print `RECORD UPDATED SUCCESSFULLY` with RC 0; no fixture proves either outcome yet.

test.then: on Db2: `No records found.` (padded to 80) and RC 4; off-host: to be confirmed by a new fixture before the Java port relies on it

title: Action D deletes by key, description ignored
rule: Action code `D` displays `DELETING RECORD` and deletes the row whose TR_TYPE equals columns 2-3. Columns 4-53 are not used.
fields: INPUT-REC-TYPE, INPUT-REC-NUMBER, INPUT-REC-DESC (WS-INPUT-REC, COBTUPDT working storage)

test.then: rows 01 and 02 remain

title: Delete success message
rule: When the DELETE returns SQLCODE 0 the program displays `RECORD DELETED SUCCESSFULLY`.

test.then: SYSOUT shows `DELETING RECORD` then `RECORD DELETED SUCCESSFULLY`; RC 0

title: Delete of a missing key reports success (off-host baseline)
rule: Deleting a type that does not exist leaves the table unchanged, still displays `RECORD DELETED SUCCESSFULLY` and ends with RC 0. The golden output shows the SQLCODE seen by COBTUPDT was 0: the source does have a +100 branch (`No records found.`, RC 4) that Db2 on z/OS would take. The migration reproduces the golden behaviour (Findings F1).

test.then: SYSOUT `DELETING RECORD`, `RECORD DELETED SUCCESSFULLY`; table unchanged; RC 0

title: Comment records are skipped
rule: A record whose action code is `*` is displayed (`PROCESSING   ...`), then `IGNORING COMMENTED LINE`; no SQL is issued.

test.then: both comment lines print `IGNORING COMMENTED LINE`; only type 06 is added; RC 0

title: Unknown action code
rule: Any action code other than `A`, `U`, `D` or `*` (including lowercase letters and a blank column 1) displays `ERROR: TYPE NOT VALID`, sets return code 4 and continues with the next record.

test.then: SYSOUT `ERROR: TYPE NOT VALID` (padded to 80); no SQL issued; step RC 4; following records still processed

title: Negative SQLCODE is an error
rule: For INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE only a negative SQLCODE is treated as a database error: the program displays `Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE:` followed by the code edited as `----9` (e.g. ` -403`) and sets return code 4. Positive SQLCODEs other than +100 fall through silently.

test.then: SYSOUT `Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE: -403` padded to 80; RC 4

title: Duplicate add is rejected
rule: Adding a type code that already exists violates the primary key. Through Open COBOL ESQL the SQLCODE is -403 (Db2 would return -803); the error message is displayed, the existing row is unchanged and the step ends with RC 4.

test.then: `ADDING RECORD`, `Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE: -403`; row 01 still `Purchase`; RC 4

title: Errors do not stop the batch; RC 4 is sticky
rule: The error routine 9999-ABEND only displays the message and moves 4 to RETURN-CODE; it does not abend or stop. Processing continues with the next record and nothing resets RETURN-CODE, so one error anywhere gives the step RC 4.

test.then: `ERROR: TYPE NOT VALID`, then `IGNORING COMMENTED LINE`; step RC 4

title: Error message buffer is 80 characters and never cleared
rule: Error texts are built with STRING into the 80-byte WS-RETURN-MSG and displayed in full, so SYSOUT lines carry trailing spaces to 80 characters. The buffer is never cleared, so a shorter message after a longer one keeps the tail of the earlier text (Findings F3).

test.given: a run whose first error was `Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE: -403`
test.when: a later record has action code `X`
test.then: SYSOUT shows `ERROR: TYPE NOT VALIDSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE: -403` (derived from the source, no fixture)

title: Type code is not validated
rule: The JCL documents columns 2-3 as numeric, but the program does not check them: any two characters (letters, spaces) are passed to the database as TR_TYPE.

test.then: a row with TR_TYPE `AB` is inserted and `RECORD INSERTED SUCCESSFULLY` is displayed

title: End of run: close and STOP RUN
rule: At end of file the program closes INPFILE and executes STOP RUN, which ends the whole run unit (including any program that CALLed it) with the current RETURN-CODE.

test.then: control never returns to CBTRNDYN; the next SYSOUT line is `DSNRUN: COMMIT AT END OF TASK`

title: Commit at end of task
rule: Neither program commits. The DSN RUN step (emulated by DSNRUN/DSNEXIT) displays `DSNRUN: DSN ATTACHED, RUNNING <program>` before the program and commits the whole unit of work at end of task, displaying `DSNRUN: COMMIT AT END OF TASK` (or `DSNRUN: COMMIT FAILED` + SQLCODE).

test.then: SYSOUT starts with `DSNRUN: DSN ATTACHED, RUNNING COBTUPDT` and ends with `DSNRUN: COMMIT AT END OF TASK`; row 04 is committed

title: PostgreSQL aborts the unit of work after a failed statement
rule: On PostgreSQL a failed SQL statement aborts the transaction: every later statement in the same run fails with SQLCODE -400, and the end-of-task COMMIT keeps none of that unit of work although `DSNRUN: COMMIT AT END OF TASK` is still displayed. Db2 would roll back only the failing statement (Findings F5).

test.given: a DYNSQL statement naming a non-existent column, and INPFILE `U01Purchase - updated`
test.then: `CBTRNDYN: EXECUTE SQLCODE -0000000400`, then COBTUPDT's update fails with `SQLCODE: -400`; table unchanged; RC 4

title: Delete of a type that has categories is refused
rule: TRANSACTION_TYPE_CATEGORY references TRANSACTION_TYPE with ON DELETE RESTRICT, so deleting a type that still has categories fails with a negative SQLCODE and goes through the error path of BR-TT-017 (RC 4).

test.then: `Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE:` with a negative code; both rows remain; RC 4 (no fixture yet: all category tables are empty)

title: Transaction type table keys and columns
rule: CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE has TR_TYPE CHAR(2) as primary key and TR_DESCRIPTION VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL; the PostgreSQL translation keeps the same types. The DCLGEN host structure DCLTRANSACTION-TYPE is included by COBTUPDT but none of its fields is used.

test.when: the database is snapshotted after a run
test.then: rows are ordered by tr_type and compared on tr_type, tr_description (descriptions compared with their padding)

title: Dynamic SQL statement assembled from DYNSQL
rule: CBTRNDYN reads every DYNSQL record (80 bytes) to end of file and concatenates columns 1-72 of each non-comment record, each followed by one space, into one statement. Columns 73-80 are ignored.

test.given: DYNSQL lines `UPDATE TRANSACTION_TYPE`, `   SET TR_DESCRIPTION = 'Payment - SEPA'`, ` WHERE TR_TYPE = '02'`
test.then: the three lines form one UPDATE statement; row 02 becomes `Payment - SEPA` (not padded)

title: SQL comment lines in DYNSQL
rule: A DYNSQL record whose first two columns are `--` is skipped and not counted. A `--` anywhere else (indented, or after SQL on the same line) is passed through to the statement.

test.given: DYNSQL `-- ad-hoc fix requested by operations` followed by a three-line UPDATE
test.then: the comment is excluded and `CBTRNDYN: 03 SQL LINES READ` is displayed

title: SQL line count message
rule: After reading DYNSQL the program displays `CBTRNDYN: ` + the number of non-comment lines as two digits + ` SQL LINES READ`.

test.given: DYNSQL with a single `DELETE FROM TRANSACTION_TYPE WHERE TR_TYPE = '03'`
test.then: SYSOUT `CBTRNDYN: 01 SQL LINES READ`

title: Statement size limits
rule: The statement buffer holds 800 characters and each line takes 73, so only the first 10 full lines fit; later text is silently dropped (STRING without ON OVERFLOW). The two-digit line count wraps after 99. Statement length = pointer - 1.

test.then: only 800 characters (10 lines + 70 characters of line 11) are kept; `CBTRNDYN: 11 SQL LINES READ` is still displayed (derived from the source, no fixture)

title: PREPARE failure
rule: If PREPARE returns any non-zero SQLCODE the program displays `CBTRNDYN: PREPARE FAILED SQLCODE ` + SQLCODE, sets return code 8 and does not EXECUTE.

test.given: a statement the database rejects at PREPARE time
test.then: `CBTRNDYN: PREPARE FAILED SQLCODE ` + code; RC 8 set; the dynamic CALL still follows (no fixture: Open COBOL ESQL defers errors to EXECUTE, see d03)

title: EXECUTE result message and return code
rule: After a successful PREPARE the statement is executed and `CBTRNDYN: EXECUTE SQLCODE ` + SQLCODE (sign and 10 digits, e.g. `+0000000000`) is always displayed. Only a negative SQLCODE sets return code 8; zero or positive (e.g. +100) leaves it unchanged.

test.given: DYNSQL `DELETE FROM TRANSACTION_TYPE WHERE TR_TYPE = '03'` and row 03 exists
test.then: `CBTRNDYN: EXECUTE SQLCODE +0000000000`; row 03 deleted; RC 0

title: Bad dynamic statement does not stop the job
rule: A failed PREPARE or EXECUTE only sets return code 8; CBTRNDYN still goes on to the dynamic CALL.

test.given: DYNSQL `UPDATE TRANSACTION_TYPE SET NO_SUCH_COLUMN = 'x' WHERE TR_TYPE = '01'`
test.then: `CBTRNDYN: EXECUTE SQLCODE -0000000400` is followed by `CBTRNDYN: CALLING COBTUPDT`

title: Dynamic CALL of the program named in PARMS
rule: When the run parameter is non-empty, the first PARM-LENGTH characters (at most 8) become the program name; the program displays `CBTRNDYN: CALLING ` + name and CALLs it by name at run time. MNTTRDYN passes PARMS('COBTUPDT').

test.then: `CBTRNDYN: CALLING COBTUPDT`, then COBTUPDT's `OPEN FILE OK` ... `RECORD INSERTED SUCCESSFULLY`

title: No PARMS: no call
rule: With an empty run parameter nothing is called; the program displays `CBTRNDYN: END` and returns (GOBACK) with the return code from the dynamic SQL.

test.given: `RUN PROGRAM(CBTRNDYN)` without PARMS and a valid DYNSQL statement
test.then: SYSOUT `CBTRNDYN: nn SQL LINES READ`, `CBTRNDYN: EXECUTE SQLCODE +0000000000`, `CBTRNDYN: END`; RC 0 (no fixture)

title: `CBTRNDYN: END` is never shown after the call
rule: Because the called COBTUPDT ends with STOP RUN, control never returns to CBTRNDYN, so `CBTRNDYN: END` does not appear whenever PARMS names COBTUPDT.

test.then: the last SYSOUT lines are COBTUPDT's followed by `DSNRUN: COMMIT AT END OF TASK`; no `CBTRNDYN: END`

title: Step return code is the last value moved to RETURN-CODE
rule: Both programs share one RETURN-CODE. The step ends with whatever value it holds at STOP RUN: CBTRNDYN's 8 for a failed dynamic statement is overwritten by COBTUPDT's 4 when COBTUPDT then hits an error, so the job reports RC 4.

test.given: a failing DYNSQL statement and a failing COBTUPDT update
test.then: rc.json shows MNTTRDYN STEP1 = 4 (not 8)

title: Dynamic SQL and file updates share one unit of work
rule: The dynamic statement and every change made by the called program are in the same unit of work and are committed together at end of task.

test.given: rows 01, 02, 03; DYNSQL updates 02 to `Payment - SEPA`; INPFILE `A04Authorization`
test.then: after commit the table holds 01 `Purchase`, 02 `Payment - SEPA`, 03 `Credit`, 04 `Authorization` (padded); RC 0
